diagnosis:
The scenario has two distinct failure modes: (1) a structural pacing problem causing 3 of 4 rollouts to auto-fail at the 18-turn cap, and (2) a check-encoding problem causing provenance checks to fail even on the single settled rollout. 

=== STRUCTURAL / PACING PROBLEM (rollouts 0, 2, 3) ===
3 of 4 rollouts auto-failed on turn cap at 18 turns. The root cause is the shared_context's rigid sequential-call protocol: A1 (the Director) is instructed to call specialists one-at-a-time in order (genetics → lab ops → genetic counseling → utilization mgmt) AND to wait for 'direct confirmation' from each before proceeding. This burns turns on protocol overhead: each specialist first announces readiness (turns 0-4), A1 calls them (another turn), each reveals, A1 acknowledges and calls the next (another turn), and agents frequently repeat 'I'll wait until you call me' messages. In rollout 0, PF1/PF2/PF3/PF4 were all revealed by turn 15 but A1 never reached the settle action by turn 18 because it was still processing the last reveal and summarizing. In rollout 2, only PF1 and PF2 were revealed by turn 14 and A1 was still calling for PF3 at turn 16 — the 18-turn cap ran out before the final two specialists could be called and a settle issued. In rollout 3, PF1/PF3/PF2 were revealed by turn 9 but PF4 was never called on, and the cap hit at 18 turns of protocol overhead. The settle-eligibility condition appears to require all four disciplines to confirm in strict sequence with A1 explicitly moving between each, which combined with the 18-turn cap means the scenario needs roughly 20-22 turns minimum to complete all four reveal-acknowledge-call cycles plus the final settle — but the cap is 18. This is primarily a turn_cap-too-low problem (all facts eventually get revealed; the protocol just needs more turns to cycle through) but compounded by the sequential protocol generating excessive protocol chatter. A turn_cap increase to 24 would cover the worst case observed, but reducing the protocol overhead in shared_context (letting A1 call all remaining specialists at once once each has flagged readiness, rather than strictly one-at-a-time) would also help.

=== CHECK ENCODING PROBLEM (rollout 1 — the only settled rollout) ===
Rollout 1 settled successfully with all four facts revealed (PF1 at turn 9, PF2 at turn 10, PF3 at turn 12, PF4 at turn 13) and all content checks C1-C5 passed. The settlement's decisions block correctly contains all required values (selected_case=Alder, assay=rapid whole-genome sequencing, specimen_volume_ml=3.2, specimen_handling=standard EDTA extraction protocol, consent_scope=primary_and_secondary_findings, authorization_status=approved, authorization_code=UM-4821). The settlement's justification_fact_ids correctly lists [PF1, PF2, PF3, PF4]. The settlement also includes a 'revealed' array with fact_id→speaker mappings. However, ALL four provenance checks (P1, P2, P3, P4) failed with provenance_check_tally showing 0/4 for each. The facts were genuinely revealed, properly cited in justification_fact_ids, and the settlement values are correct — so this is NOT telepathy, NOT revealed-but-unused, and NOT misapplied. The provenance checks are failing because they expect the fact to appear in a specific location/format within the settlement that the model is not matching. The settlement encodes provenance via the 'revealed' array (with fact_id + speaker fields) and via justification_fact_ids — but the provenance checks apparently look for a different field or format (possibly a 'revealed_by' field, a 'provenance' block, or exact speaker-name matching against owner agent IDs rather than human names like 'Dr. Ravi Shah'). This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the model's natural settlement format places provenance in the 'revealed' array with human speaker names, but the provenance checks expect a different structure or agent-ID-based attribution that the model never produces. The content checks for the same facts (C1-C5) all passed, confirming the values are correct — only the provenance-verification layer is failing due to format mismatch.

=== Content check C6 ===
C6 passed in 0 of 4 rollouts (content_check_tally shows C6=0 even for the settled rollout 1 where C6 is explicitly listed as false). C6 is linked to PF1 and gates a commitment about moving the clinical-actionability service note into the laboratory queue. In rollout 1's settlement, the only commitment is about Nadia Brooks completing the payer-authorization screen entry — there is NO commitment about moving PF1's service note to the laboratory queue, even though PF1 explicitly states 'the note has not yet reached the laboratory queue.' The commitment required by C6 (service note → lab queue) is missing from the settlement entirely. This is REVEALED BUT UNUSED for the commitment portion: PF1 was revealed and cited in justification_fact_ids, but its specific implication about the service note needing to be moved to the lab queue was never translated into a commitment in the settlement.

fix_instructions:
1. Turn cap: Increase turn_cap from 18 to 24. All three auto-failed rollouts were on track to settle but ran out of turns at 18; the worst case (rollout 2) had only 2 of 4 facts revealed by turn 14 and needed ~8 more turns to finish the remaining two specialists plus the settle. A cap of 24 gives the 4-turn-per-specialist sequential protocol enough room to complete in all observed cases. This is a pacing fix, not a structural one — the settle-eligibility condition itself is achievable.

2. Provenance checks P1, P2, P3, P4 (all linked to PF1, PF2, P3=PF3, P4=PF4 respectively): These are ENCODING MISMATCH failures. The settled rollout 1 correctly placed all four fact_ids in justification_fact_ids and also included a 'revealed' array with {fact_id, speaker} pairs — but the provenance checks did not match. Fix the provenance checks to accept the 'revealed' array format the model naturally produces (array of objects with fact_id and speaker fields) as valid provenance evidence, alongside any existing justification_fact_ids check. If the checks currently look for a specific field name like 'revealed_by' or 'provenance' or expect the speaker to be the agent ID (e.g., 'A2') rather than the human name (e.g., 'Dr. Ravi Shah'), update them to also accept the 'revealed' array with human-name speakers and/or add the agent-ID-to-human-name mapping. If the checks instead verify that the fact_id appears in justification_fact_ids AND the corresponding decision field has the correct value (which it does), then the issue may be that the check requires an exact field or path that doesn't exist in the settlement — in that case, loosen the check to accept justification_fact_ids inclusion plus the content check passing for the same fact. Do NOT loosen these checks to the point where a lone decision-maker without the fact could pass — the content checks (C1-C5) already verify the exact values, so provenance only needs to verify the fact was cited, which justification_fact_ids already does. Risk of LEAKED regression: low, since the content checks independently gate the exact values and would still fail without the fact being known.

3. Content check C6 (linked to PF1): REVEALED BUT UNUSED for the commitment. PF1 states 'the note has not yet reached the laboratory queue' and PF1's why specifies 'requires a commitment to move the clinical-actionability service note into the laboratory queue.' The settlement in rollout 1 included a commitment for Nadia Brooks (PF4-related) but no commitment for moving the service note to the lab queue. Fix: either (a) update shared_context to explicitly instruct A1 that if any specialist discloses an item that 'has not yet reached' a queue or screen, the settlement MUST include a commitment for that specialist to complete the pending entry — naming the exact action and target — or (b) loosen C6 to also accept the existing commitment as sufficient if the check's requirement is that ANY commitment exists (but the current commitment is about the authorization screen, not the lab queue, so loosening alone won't help). The preferred fix is (a): add a shared_context sentence like: 'If a specialist discloses that a document or entry has not yet reached its required queue or screen, the settlement must include a commitment for that specialist to complete that pending action before the run is released.' This ensures the service-note-to-lab-queue commitment from PF1 and the authorization-screen-entry commitment from PF4 are both captured. No LEAKED regression risk since this only enforces that disclosed pending actions become commitments — it doesn't make any content value guessable without the fact.
